Use case: historical-scene. Create one full-color photorealistic cinematic image from a THREE-IMAGE SET depicting the SAME ordinary Ahom village imagined in Upper Assam circa 1450, using the user-approved Shan comparative house and clothing references. This is an artistic reconstruction, not authenticated period evidence. Maintain one consistent village identity: a gently curving earthen main lane, a small irregular oval pond beside its central junction, a particularly large long house with a round-ended roof and vine on its end-veranda near that junction, domestic bamboo-fenced yards, a few branching footpaths, bamboo groves around the west edge, rice paddies beyond the east edge. A compact believable settlement of roughly 25–35 household buildings, with varied sizes and orientations rather than a military grid. The defining house architecture: long ridge, deep thick grass thatch, rounded hipped roof end below a small triangular gable opening, low sweeping eaves, hardwood posts, woven bamboo panels, an end veranda, some enclosed ground-level workspaces and small lean-to shelters. Related house variants should clearly belong to the same local building vocabulary, not identical clones. Clothing: men in simple charcoal/indigo or pale front-fastening jackets, loose knee- or calf-length trousers, broad dark round woven hats or occasional cloth headwraps, diagonal woven shoulder bags. Adult women in dark fitted upper wraps, long wrapped skirts with subdued rust-brown patterned bands and broad cream lower bands, light shoulder cloths; a few wear broad-brimmed woven hats with tall pointed crowns inspired by the woman's supplied portrait. Appropriate natural scale, distinct faces, everyday domestic and farm activity, no staged ethnic group portrait. Baskets, earthen pots, firewood, rice mats, chickens, simple hand tools; humid green flat Assam valley, banana and broadleaf trees, bamboo, light morning haze, warm early morning sun, consistent restrained green/cream/indigo/earth-brown palette. Photographic natural texture and depth, outstanding realistic thatch and bamboo detail, landscape 16:9. This is a common village, not a palace or fortified royal precinct. No temple towers, shrines or deity reliefs imported into house design, no pagodas or swept Chinese temple roofs, no surviving later masonry monuments, no concrete, metal sheets, plastic, poles or wires, asphalt, vehicles, rifles, modern flags, dhoti-kurta substituted for the supplied Shan costumes, maize, tea plantations, text, watermarks, borders or collage. Each output must be ONE continuous scene, never a triptych or contact sheet.

IMAGE 1 OF 3 — COMPLETE VILLAGE OVERVIEW. Input image 1: previously generated village street, main visual reference for house forms, colors and people. Input image 2: user's Shan house drawing, structural comparative reference only. Input images 3 and 4: Shan men's and woman's clothing photographs, costume comparisons only. View from a moderately elevated oblique position about 20–30 meters above ground at the southwest edge, wide cinematic composition showing the COMPLETE settlement from nearest fenced household yards through branching lane and central pond to the last homes and surrounding fields. Reveal clear spatial relationships and everyday scale, not hundreds of oversized roofs. Keep the round-ended roof shapes visible. Include the large vine-veranda house near the central junction and pond. Small scattered villagers work and walk, rice mats in yards, a farmer with a buffalo near outer paddies, simple timber footbridges over drainage ditches. No grand village hall resembling a palace, no fortress, no oversized ceremonial gate. Trees should frame and interweave the houses, not obscure the village. Horizon remains low and hazy; settlement fills most of the frame. A visually coherent substantial inhabited village, not a handful of huts.
